Add a generic implementation of Speck
Speck64 variants.  Speck is a lightweight block cipher that can be much
faster than AES on processors that don't have AES instructions.
We are planning to offer Speck-XTS (probably Speck128/256-XTS) as an
option for dm-crypt and fscrypt on Android
with older CPUs such as ARMv7 which don't have the Cryptography
Extensions.  Currently
column2: such devices are unencrypted because AES is not

column1: fast enough
column2: even when the NEON bit-sliced implementation of AES is

column1: used.  Other AES alternatives such as Twofish
CAST6
column2: and Serpent aren't fast enough either; it seems that only a

column1: modern ARX cipher can provide sufficient performance on these devices.
This is a replacement for our original proposal
(https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/10101451/) which was to offer
ChaCha20 for these devices.  However
column2: the use of a stream cipher for

column1: disk/file encryption with no space to store nonces would have been much
more insecure than we thought initially
column2: given that it would be used on

column1: top of flash storage as well as potentially on top of F2FS
which is guaranteed to overwrite data in-place.
Speck has been somewhat controversial due to its origin.  Nevertheless
it has a straightforward design (it's an ARX cipher)
be the leading software-optimized lightweight block cipher currently
with the most cryptanalysis.  It's also easy to implement without side
channels
column3: we only intend Speck to be used when

column1: the status quo is no encryption
column2: due to AES not being fast enough.

column1: We've also considered a novel length-preserving encryption mode based on
ChaCha20 and Poly1305.  While theoretically attractive
would be a brand new crypto construction and would be more complicated
and difficult to implement efficiently in comparison to Speck-XTS.
There is confusion about the byte and word orders of Speck
original paper doesn't specify them.  But we have implemented it using
the orders the authors recommended in a correspondence with them.  The
test vectors are taken from the original paper but were mapped to byte
arrays using the recommended byte and word orders.
